item.text: {"text":"Mean pooling is permutation invariant: identical token multisets produce identical text vectors, so it cannot represent phrase order, negation scope, or which dimension belongs to which attribute. It can still distinguish different identifiers or numbers when tokenization preserves them. Unordered encoders can perform strongly on classification benchmarks ([Iyyer et al., 2015](https://aclanthology.org/P15-1162/)), but that does not establish these specific capabilities. Character CNNs learn orthographic and morphological features with shared parameters ([Kim et al., 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.06615)); this supports testing them for product strings, not claiming demonstrated numerical understanding. A character CNN applied separately to words followed by unordered word pooling still loses phrase order. Retrieved sequential-recommendation work such as [ITS-Rec](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) uses pretrained BERT and reviews, so its results do not establish gains under this task’s restrictions.\n\nFocused hypothesis: replace the mean-pooled text branch with a small character CNN operating across each title/description, preserving punctuation, digits and spaces, then project its pooled features into the existing item-ID representation. Train everything jointly from random initialization within one HSTU model per category. Local filters can distinguish ordered substrings within their receptive field; global pooling still limits long-range relationships and negation scope. Compare against mean pooling with matched total trainable parameters, identical text coverage/truncation, backbone, objective, sampling, seeds and training budget. Report macro validation HR@10, per-category results, training-frequency strata and runtime. Add controlled text-vector checks for reordered phrases, negation and dimensions; these diagnose representational sensitivity, not recommendation accuracy. No retrieved source establishes a parameter- and frequency-controlled winner for this exact setting."}
